content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "Nowadays more and more college students have come to realize social practice and academic learning are equally important." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.

modelEssay.title: Social Practice and Academic Learning
modelEssay.content:
Nowadays more and more college students have come to realize social practice and academic learning are equally important. This belief stems from the understanding that a well-rounded education involves both theoretical knowledge and practical skills.

In the realm of academic learning, students delve into textbooks and lectures, acquiring the foundational knowledge that forms the basis of their future professions. However, this theoretical framework is often insufficient to prepare them for the complexities of the real world. Social practice, on the other hand, offers a complementary experience. It allows students to apply their academic knowledge in real-life scenarios, fostering critical thinking and problem-solving abilities. For instance, a business student might learn about market analysis in class, but it is through internships and case studies that they truly grasp the dynamics of the market.

In conclusion, the synergy between social practice and academic learning is indispensable for the holistic development of college students. It is through this balance that students can bridge the gap between theory and practice, equipping themselves with the competencies necessary to thrive in their future careers.

transcript.text: Mr.

transcript.speaker: F

transcript.text: Just how did you achieve this?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 您究竟是如何做到这一点的？

transcript.text: The achievement belongs to all the residents of Birkton.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这项成就属于伯克顿的所有居民。

transcript.text: It was a shared effort, where everybody pitched in for the communal good.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这是共同努力的结果，每个人都为了共同利益而贡献力量。

transcript.text: But how did this change happen?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但这种变化是如何发生的呢？

transcript.translation: 在大约十年间，伯克顿从一个相对默默无闻、沉睡的村庄变成了一个必去的旅游目的地。

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 伯克顿一直很幸运，拥有如此美丽的自然魅力。

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这一转变始于2008年春天的一次市政厅会议——那是十多年前的事了——当时绝大多数邻居投票支持836号动议。

transcript.text: This legislative proposal essentially set out to harmonise the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Birkton.

transcript.translation: 这项立法提案本质上旨在协调伯克顿所有房屋的外观美感。

transcript.text: The idea was that if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features, then a village as a whole would look more beautiful.

transcript.text: And it worked.

transcript.text: It certainly did.

transcript.translation: 确实如此。

transcript.text: I'm looking now at a before and after photo, and the change is truly remarkable.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我现在在看一张前后对比照片，变化确实非常显著。

transcript.text: Researchers in the US have created a remote-controlled robot that is so small it can walk on the top of a US penny.

transcript.text: 5mm wide.
transcript.translation: 5毫米宽。

transcript.text: Researchers described it as the smallest ever remote-controlled walking robot.
transcript.translation: 研究人员将其描述为有史以来最小的遥控行走机器人。

transcript.text: The tiny robot can bend, twist, crawl, walk, turn and even jump without the use of complex hardware or special power.
transcript.translation: 这种微型机器人能够弯曲、扭转、爬行、行走、转弯甚至跳跃，无需使用复杂硬件或特殊电源。

transcript.text: The engineers said this is because the robot is powered by the elastic property of its body.
transcript.translation: 工程师们表示，这是因为机器人由其身体的弹性特性提供动力。

transcript.text: To construct the robot, the researchers used a shape-memory alloy material that transforms to its remembered shape when heated.
transcript.translation: 为了构造这种机器人，研究人员使用了一种形状记忆合金材料，该材料在受热时会变形成记忆形状。

transcript.text: Using a laser, the team is able to heat the robot at specific parts of its body, causing it to change shape.
transcript.translation: 通过使用激光，团队能够在机器人的特定部位进行加热，使其改变形状。

transcript.text: As the robot deforms and goes back to its original shape, it creates movement from one place to another.
transcript.translation: 当机器人变形并恢复到原始形状时，它会产生从一个地方到另一个地方的移动。

transcript.text: Because these structures are so tiny, the rate of cooling is very fast, Project Lead Professor John A.
transcript.translation: 由于这些结构非常小，冷却速度非常快，项目负责人约翰·A。

transcript.text: While the research is still in the exploratory phase, the team believes that technology could lead to micro-sized robots that can perform practical tasks in tightly confined spaces.
transcript.translation: 虽然研究仍处于探索阶段，但团队相信这项技术可以开发出能够在狭窄受限空间中执行实际任务的微型机器人。

transcript.text: You might imagine micro-robots as agents to repair or assemble small structures or machines in industry, or as surgical assistants to clear clogged arteries, to stop internal bleeding, or to eliminate cancerous tumors, all in minimally invasive procedures, Rogers said.

transcript.text: I don't want to boast or anything, but I have always considered myself something of an elite sleeper.
transcript.translation: 我不想自夸什么，但我一直认为自己算是个精英睡眠者。

transcript.text: Given the opportunity, I will sleep for marathon stretches and can doze through the most extreme situations.
transcript.translation: 只要有机会，我会进行马拉松式的长时间睡眠，甚至能在最极端的情况下打盹。

transcript.text: On one very rough ferry crossing, on the route to the Isles of Scilly, for example, my traveling companion spent the entire three-hour ride throwing up in the bathroom, while I dozed happily on a plastic chair.
transcript.translation: 例如，在前往锡利群岛的一次非常颠簸的渡轮穿越中，我的旅伴在整个三小时的旅程中都在卫生间呕吐，而我却在塑料椅上愉快地打盹。

transcript.text: Unfortunately, it has come to my attention that I am not an elite sleeper after all.
transcript.translation: 不幸的是，我意识到自己其实并不是一个精英睡眠者。

transcript.text: It seems I am just lazy, because elite sleepers are defined as the approximately 3% of the population who are biologically programmed to need less sleep than the rest of us.
transcript.translation: 看来我只是懒惰，因为精英睡眠者被定义为大约3%的人口，他们在生物学上被设定为比其他人需要更少的睡眠。

transcript.text: According to a study that came out in March, elite sleepers have rare genetic changes, which means they can sleep fewer hours than mere mortals without any risk of cognitive decline.
transcript.translation: 根据三月份发布的一项研究，精英睡眠者拥有罕见的基因变化，这意味着他们比普通人睡眠时间更少，却没有认知衰退的风险。

transcript.text: It may not be possible to change your own genes, but can you train yourself to need less sleep?
transcript.translation: 改变自己的基因可能不可能，但你能训练自己需要更少的睡眠吗？

transcript.text: Is there a non-biological way to reach elite sleeper status?
transcript.translation: 有没有一种非生物学的方式达到精英睡眠者的状态？

transcript.text: I have spent the past year trying to answer that question.
transcript.translation: 过去一年，我一直在试图回答这个问题。

transcript.text: Not for fun, I should add, but because having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep, for which I still have a great passion.
transcript.translation: 我得补充，不是为了好玩，而是因为生孩子严重扰乱了我的睡眠，而我仍然对睡眠充满热情。

transcript.text: For a while, I assumed I'd be forced to become one of those people who jump out of bed at the crack of dawn.
transcript.translation: 有一段时间，我以为自己会被迫成为那些黎明时分就跳下床的人之一。

transcript.text: After a year of tough scientific study, however, I have discovered being forced to get up early in the morning is very different from being an early bird.
transcript.translation: 然而，经过一年的艰苦科学研究，我发现被迫早起与早起者是截然不同的。

transcript.translation: 听力1。

transcript.text: If you read an article about a controversial issue, do you think you'd realise if it had changed your beliefs?
transcript.translation: 如果你读一篇关于一个有争议问题的文章，你认为你会意识到它是否改变了你的信念吗？

transcript.text: No one knows your own mind like you do.
transcript.translation: 没有人比你更了解你自己的想法。

transcript.text: It seems obvious that you would know if your beliefs had shifted.
transcript.translation: 似乎很明显，如果你的信念发生了转变，你会知道的。

transcript.text: And yet, a new paper in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests that we actually have very poor awareness of our own belief change, meaning that we will tend to underestimate how much we've been swayed by a convincing article.
transcript.translation: 然而，《实验心理学季刊》上的一篇新论文表明，我们实际上对自己信念变化的意识非常差，这意味着我们往往会低估一篇有说服力的文章对我们产生了多大影响。

transcript.text: The researchers recruited over 200 undergraduates across two studies and focused on their beliefs about whether physical punishment of kids is an effective form of discipline.
transcript.translation: 研究人员在两个研究中招募了200多名本科生，并专注于他们对体罚儿童是否是一种有效的管教方式的信念。

transcript.text: The students reported their initial beliefs about whether physical punishment is an effective way to discipline a child, on a scale from 1, completely disbelieve, to 9, completely believe.
transcript.translation: 学生们报告了他们对体罚是否是一种有效管教方式的最初信念，使用一个从1（完全不相信）到9（完全相信）的量表。

transcript.text: Several weeks later, they were given one of two research-based texts to read.
transcript.translation: 几周后，他们被给予两篇基于研究的文本之一来阅读。

transcript.text: Each was several pages long and either presented the arguments and data in favour of physical punishment or against it.
transcript.translation: 每篇文本长达几页，要么支持体罚的论据和数据，要么反对体罚的论据和数据。

transcript.text: After this, the students answered some questions to test their comprehension and memory of the text.
transcript.translation: 之后，学生们回答了一些问题以测试他们对文本的理解和记忆。

transcript.text: Then, the students again scored their belief in whether physical punishment is effective or not.
transcript.translation: 然后，学生们再次评估他们对体罚是否有效的信念。

transcript.text: Finally, the researchers asked them to recall what their belief had been at the start of the study.
transcript.translation: 最后，研究人员要求他们回忆研究开始时他们的信念是什么。

transcript.text: The students' belief about physical punishment changed when they read a text that argued against their own initial position.
transcript.translation: 当学生们阅读一篇反对他们自己最初立场的文本时，他们对体罚的信念发生了变化。

transcript.text: Crucially, the memory of their initial belief was shifted in the direction of their new belief.
transcript.translation: 关键的是，他们对最初信念的记忆朝着新信念的方向发生了偏移。

transcript.text: In fact, their memory was closer to their current belief than their original belief.
transcript.translation: 事实上，他们的记忆更接近他们当前的信念，而不是他们最初的信念。

transcript.text: The more their belief had changed, the larger this memory bias tended to be, suggesting the students were relying on their current belief to deduce their initial belief.
transcript.translation: 他们的信念变化越大，这种记忆偏差就越大，这表明学生们依靠他们当前的信念来推断他们最初的信念。

transcript.text: The memory bias was unrelated to the measures of how well they'd understood or recalled the text, suggesting these factors didn't play a role in memory of initial belief or awareness of belief change.
transcript.translation: 记忆偏差与他们理解或回忆文本程度的测量无关，这表明这些因素在最初信念的记忆或信念变化的意识中不起作用。

transcript.text: The researchers concede that this research was about changes to mostly moderate beliefs.
transcript.translation: 研究人员承认，这项研究主要关注的是对大多中等信念的变化。

transcript.text: It's likely the findings would be different in the context of changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs.
transcript.translation: 在极端或根深蒂固的信念发生变化的情况下，研究结果可能会有所不同。

transcript.text: However, our beliefs on most topics are in the moderate range, and as we go about our daily lives reading informative material, these intriguing findings suggest we are mostly ignorant of how what we just read has updated and altered our own position.
transcript.translation: 然而，我们对大多数话题的信念都处于中等范围，而且当我们在日常生活中阅读有信息量的材料时，这些引人入胜的发现表明，我们大多忽视了刚才阅读的内容如何更新和改变了我们自己的立场。

transcript.text: As the American population grows, so does the number of American moms.
transcript.translation: 随着美国人口的增长，美国妈妈的数量也在增加。

transcript.text: But more than a century after Mother's Day became an official holiday, even as that number increases, the share of the American population who are mothers is at the lowest point in a quarter century.
transcript.translation: 但在母亲节成为法定节日一个多世纪后，即使这个数字在增加，美国人口中母亲的比例却处于二十五年来的最低点。

transcript.text: It's frequently noted that fertility rates are falling sharply in richer countries, but the less observed consequence of this trend is that a decline in births can also mean a decline in motherhood in general.
transcript.translation: 人们经常注意到，富裕国家的生育率急剧下降，但这一趋势较少被观察到的后果是，出生率的下降也可能意味着整体母亲身份的减少。

transcript.text: According to my analysis of data from the Census Bureau, the decline of American motherhood is real, occurring very quickly, and may continue for some time yet.
transcript.translation: 根据我对人口普查局数据的分析，美国母亲身份的减少是真实的，发生得非常快，并且可能还会持续一段时间。

transcript.text: Not only are moms making up less of the population, but their characteristics are changing too, and in a way that might be linked to their proportional decline.
transcript.translation: 不仅妈妈在人口中的比例下降，她们的特征也在变化，并且这种变化可能与其比例下降有关。

transcript.text: Moms today tend to be than in the past.
transcript.translation: 今天的妈妈往往比过去更年长。

transcript.text: Just looking at recent years, the change in age-specific birth rates has been drastic.
transcript.translation: 仅看最近几年，特定年龄出生率的变化非常剧烈。

transcript.text: In just the past few years, the peak childbearing age range for American women has advanced from that of 25 to 29 to that of 30 to 34.
transcript.translation: 就在过去几年里，美国女性的生育高峰年龄段已经从25至29岁推进到30至34岁。

transcript.text: Meanwhile, childbearing among women under 20 has fallen by half or more, while childbearing among women 35 and older is rising.
transcript.translation: 与此同时，20岁以下女性的生育率下降了一半或更多，而35岁及以上女性的生育率正在上升。

transcript.text: One positive consequence of this age shift is that a larger proportion of new mothers are economically prepared to raise children.
transcript.translation: 这种年龄转变的一个积极后果是，更大比例的新妈妈在经济上做好了抚养孩子的准备。

transcript.text: Less positively, however, many women find that, as they age, they can't have as many kids as they would like.
transcript.translation: 然而，不那么积极的是，许多女性发现，随着年龄增长，她们无法生育如她们所愿数量的孩子。

transcript.text: Plus, having children later in life can increase the risk of health complications.
transcript.translation: 此外，晚育可能会增加健康并发症的风险。

transcript.text: These finer points aside, one major consequence of the older mom's trend is that fewer years of a woman's life are spent as a mother.
transcript.translation: 撇开这些细微之处不谈，妈妈老龄化趋势的一个主要后果是，女性作为母亲的生活年数减少了。

transcript.text: This means that, at any given time, a larger share of women, and thus of the whole population, will report not having children in government surveys.
transcript.translation: 这意味着，在任何给定时间，更大比例的女性，从而也是整个人口，将在政府调查中报告没有孩子。

transcript.text: In other words, later motherhood means less motherhood.
transcript.translation: 换句话说，晚育意味着母亲身份的减少。

transcript.text: Even as motherhood rates decline, Mother's Day, of course, will endure.
transcript.translation: 即使母亲身份比率下降，母亲节当然会持续存在。

transcript.text: In fact, despite the demographic shift, retail spending on the holiday appears to be rising.
transcript.translation: 事实上，尽管人口结构发生变化，母亲节的零售支出似乎在上升。

transcript.text: It is hard to say if Mother's Day spending is rising more than one would expect, given that the American population keeps growing.
transcript.translation: 很难说母亲节的支出是否超出了人们的预期，鉴于美国人口持续增长。

transcript.text: But one factor might be that the proportion of women who are the mothers of adult children is rising, and those adult children may spend more generously when it comes to celebrating the moms they no longer live with.
transcript.translation: 但一个因素可能是，作为成年子女母亲的女性比例正在上升，而这些成年子女在庆祝他们不再同住的母亲时可能花费更慷慨。

transcript.text: Since NASA published a paper in 1989 claiming that houseplants can soak up pollution and toxic chemicals, businesses and homeowners have increasingly invested in greenery to help clean their air.
transcript.translation: 自从NASA在1989年发表论文声称室内植物可以吸收污染和有毒化学物质以来，企业和房主越来越多地投资于绿化，以帮助清洁空气。

transcript.text: But a new analysis suggests it could actually take more than 1,000 plants per square meter to gain a benefit any greater than simply opening a couple of windows.
transcript.translation: 但一项新的分析表明，实际上可能需要每平方米超过1000株植物，才能获得比仅仅打开几扇窗户更大的好处。

transcript.text: The problem lies in the fact that NASA conducted their tests in sealed containers that do not simulate the conditions in most people's homes or offices.
transcript.translation: 问题在于NASA在密封容器中进行了测试，这些容器没有模拟大多数人家庭或办公室的条件。

transcript.text: The space agency was primarily concerned about keeping the air fresh for astronauts cut off in biospheres or space stations, and helping to combat sick building syndrome, which had become a problem due to the super-insulated and energy-efficient offices of the late 1970s.
transcript.translation: 该航天机构主要关注为隔离在生物圈或空间站中的宇航员保持空气新鲜，并帮助对抗病态建筑综合症，这种综合症是由于20世纪70年代末超级隔热和节能的办公室而成为问题。

transcript.text: By the early 1980s, workers regularly complained of skin rashes, sleepiness, headaches, and allergies as they breathed in toxic chemicals from paints and plastics.
transcript.translation: 到20世纪80年代初，工人们经常抱怨皮疹、嗜睡、头痛和过敏，因为他们吸入了来自油漆和塑料的有毒化学物质。

transcript.text: NASA found that certain plants could remove chemicals from the air, and even today garden centers recommend the plants for air cleaning properties.
transcript.translation: NASA发现某些植物可以从空气中去除化学物质，甚至今天园艺中心仍推荐这些植物用于空气净化。

transcript.text: However, a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years found that houseplants in a normal environment have little impact.
transcript.translation: 然而，一项对跨越30年的数十项研究的新评估发现，在正常环境中，室内植物的影响很小。

transcript.text: In fact, natural ventilation is far better at cleaning the air.
transcript.translation: 事实上，自然通风在清洁空气方面要好得多。

transcript.text: The researchers also calculated the clean air delivery rate for plants in the studies they analyzed, and found that the rate at which plants disperse the compounds was well below the usual rate of air exchange in a normal building, caused by the movement of people coming and going, opening doors and windows.
transcript.translation: 研究人员还计算了他们分析的研究中植物的清洁空气输出率，发现植物分散化合物的速度远低于正常建筑中由人员进出、开门开窗引起的通常空气交换率。

transcript.text: Many of the studies did show a reduction in the concentration of volatile organic compounds over time, which is likely why people have seized on them to praise the air-purifying virtues of plants.
transcript.translation: 许多研究确实显示挥发性有机化合物的浓度随时间降低，这可能是人们抓住这些研究来赞美植物空气净化功效的原因。

transcript.text: But the researchers' calculations showed it would take 10 to 1,000 plants per square meter of floor space to compete with the air-cleaning capacity of a building's air handling system, or even just a couple of open windows in a house.
transcript.translation: 但研究人员的计算显示，需要每平方米地板面积10到1000株植物，才能与建筑空气处理系统的清洁能力竞争，或者甚至只是与房子中几扇打开的窗户竞争。

transcript.text: In contrast, NASA's SEALED experiment recommended one pot plant per 100 square feet.
transcript.translation: 相比之下，NASA的SEALED实验推荐每100平方英尺放置一盆植物。

transcript.text: This is certainly an example of how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time, but it's also a great example of how scientific research should continually re-examine and question findings to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what's actually happening.
transcript.translation: 这当然是科学发现如何随着时间被误导或误解的一个例子，但它也是科学研究应如何不断重新审视和质疑发现以更接近理解实际情况真相的一个好例子。

transcript.text: Questions 23 to 25 are based on the lecture you have just heard.
transcript.translation: 问题23到25基于你刚才听到的讲座。

transcript.translation: 问题23。据称NASA 1989年论文中报告的研究有什么问题？

transcript.translation: 问题24。对跨越30年的数十项研究的新评估的发现是什么？

transcript.translation: 问题25。NASA的SEALED实验建议在科学家追求真理中体现了什么？听力理解到此结束。

questionGroups.title: These are the habits to avoid if you want to make a behavior change

material.title: These are the habits to avoid if you want to make a behavior change

paragraphs.text: According to recent research, behavioral change involves physical changes in the brain. In the past decade, researchers have shown that when it comes to the duration of making a new behavior a deep-rooted habit there is not a simple answer. Even for the most productive and disciplined among us, undoing something that has become an automatic part of who we are takes more than an overnight effort. Once we've successfully made that change, we then have to make other adjustments to our lives to ensure that we continue to maintain it, which is often a whole other challenge in itself.
paragraphs.translation: 根据最近的研究，行为改变涉及大脑的物理变化。在过去的十年中，研究人员表明，当谈到使新行为成为根深蒂固的习惯所需的时间时，并没有一个简单的答案。即使对于我们中最高效和自律的人来说，改变已经成为我们自动部分的东西也需要多于一夜的努力。一旦我们成功地做出了改变，我们还需要对生活进行其他调整，以确保我们继续维持它，这本身往往就是另一个挑战。

paragraphs.text: At its core, success in changing and maintaining a behavior rarely occurs without the introduction of some sort of system. When there isn't the right framework in place, we face a greater likelihood of derailing our hard-earned progress. To ensure success in changing and maintaining a behavior, we should stay away from some detrimental habits.
paragraphs.translation: 从本质上讲，成功改变和维持行为很少在不引入某种系统的情况下发生。当没有合适的框架时，我们面临更高的可能性会破坏我们辛苦取得的进展。为了确保在改变和维持行为中取得成功，我们应该远离一些有害的习惯。

paragraphs.text: The first one to avoid is relying on willpower. Think about the last time you vowed to resist a temptation. Perhaps you didn't want to check your phone every 15 minutes, or you were determined not to reach for a chocolate bar at 3 p.m. Think about how difficult it must have been not to glance at your phone when it was within reach, or not to walk to the vending machine when your afternoon slump hit.
paragraphs.translation: 第一个要避免的是依赖意志力。想想你上次发誓抵制诱惑的时候。也许你不想每15分钟查看一次手机，或者你下定决心不在下午3点拿巧克力棒。想想当手机就在触手可及时，不瞥一眼它有多难，或者当下午低潮来袭时，不去自动售货机有多难。

paragraphs.text: The research on whether we have finite or infinite willpower is inconclusive, but experts do generally agree that you can't change and sustain a habit if you rely on your willpower alone. The old military saying "You never rise to the occasion, you only sink to the level of training" also applies to behavior change. The idea is simple—you repeat something so many times that it becomes automatic.
paragraphs.translation: 关于我们拥有有限还是无限意志力的研究尚无定论，但专家们普遍认为，如果你仅依赖意志力，你无法改变和维持一个习惯。古老的军事格言“你永远不会超常发挥，你只会退缩到训练水平”也适用于行为改变。这个想法很简单——你重复某件事很多次，直到它变得自动。

paragraphs.text: Think about what else you can change about your surroundings that makes it easier for you to perform this change on a daily basis. This is called your "cue." Basically, it's a trigger to perform that particular habit. If you don't want to reach for a sugary treat at 3 p.m., have a box of herbal tea ready at your desk. When 3 p.m. comes around, that's your cue to pour yourself a cup of hot water and drink that tea, instead of walking to the vending machine.
paragraphs.translation: 想想你还能改变环境中的什么，使你每天更容易执行这个改变。这被称为你的“提示”。基本上，它是触发特定习惯的信号。如果你不想在下午3点拿含糖零食，就在桌上准备一盒草药茶。当下午3点来临时，那就是你给自己倒一杯热水、喝茶的提示，而不是走向自动售货机。

paragraphs.text: The second one to avoid is focusing on negative goals. Sometimes, it's not your process that lets you down, but the habit that you want to change in the first place. For starters, not eating chocolate to beat your afternoon slump is a harder goal than swapping chocolate for herbal tea when you reach the designated time. Your brain wants to find routines that have succeeded in the past and allow you to repeat those actions again in the future without having to think about them explicitly. However, this habit-learning system isn't so effective when it comes to learning not to do something. That's why rather than giving up something, think about introducing something in its place. Focus on actions you are going to take that will ultimately conflict with the behaviors you want to stop. When your attention is on doing something new, you give your habit system a chance to operate.
paragraphs.translation: 第二个要避免的是专注于负面目标。有时，让你失望的不是你的过程，而是你首先想要改变的习惯。对于初学者来说，不吃巧克力来战胜下午低潮比在指定时间将巧克力换成草药茶更难。你的大脑想要找到过去成功的常规，并允许你在未来再次重复这些动作，而无需明确思考。然而，这个习惯学习系统在学习不做某事时并不那么有效。这就是为什么与其放弃某物，不如考虑引入替代物。专注于你将要采取的行动，这些行动最终会与你想停止的行为冲突。当你的注意力放在做新事情上时，你就给了习惯系统一个运作的机会。

paragraphs.text: The third one to avoid is using the same strategies in different circumstances. Because we are creatures of habit, it's natural to assume that when we do manage to adopt and sustain a desirable behavior, that same strategy will work when we want to make another behavior change. But that's not always the case. Sometimes, the system that got you to change one behavior might not work for another.
paragraphs.translation: 第三个要避免的是在不同情况下使用相同的策略。因为我们是习惯的生物，自然地会假设当我们成功采纳和维持一个理想行为时，相同的策略在我们想要进行另一个行为改变时也会奏效。但情况并非总是如此。有时，让你改变一个行为的系统可能对另一个行为无效。

paragraphs.text: Sometimes we become accustomed to relying on our guts when it comes to decision-making. This serves us well in certain situations, but can hinder us in others especially when we need to consider metrics and data, rather than letting our instinct override everything. For example, if you want to stop checking your email first thing in the morning, you might decide to substitute another activity in its place. But if you want to stop indulging in video games, simply deciding you will go for a run might not be as effective. You might need to introduce another reinforcement, such as meeting a friend and booking an exercise class together.
paragraphs.translation: 有时我们习惯于在决策时依赖直觉。这在某些情况下对我们很有用，但在其他情况下可能会阻碍我们，特别是当我们需要考虑指标和数据，而不是让本能覆盖一切时。例如，如果你想停止早上第一件事查看邮件，你可能会决定用另一个活动替代。但如果你想停止沉迷于电子游戏，仅仅决定去跑步可能不那么有效。你可能需要引入另一个强化，比如约朋友见面并一起预订一个健身课程。

paragraphs.text: The fourth one to avoid is not forgiving ourselves for slipping up. Of course, even the best-laid plans fail sometimes. You might have stuck to your screen-free nighttime routine for five days, and then a big project landed on your desk and you found yourself in bed with your laptop before you went to sleep. Or you prepared meals on Sunday and stuck to eating healthy dinners at home, but by Friday you found yourself so exhausted and opted to order greasy takeout. Life happens and even if your behavior change is small, every single day can prove pretty inflexible, and at some point your luck may run out, even if just for a day. The perfectionist in you might be screaming to abandon your goals altogether, but try to see it in the bigger picture. Just because you might have temporarily strayed off course doesn't mean you can't start afresh the next day.
paragraphs.translation: 第四个要避免的是不原谅自己的失误。当然，即使是最周密的计划有时也会失败。你可能坚持了五天的无屏幕夜间习惯，然后一个大项目落到你桌上，你发现自己在睡前把笔记本电脑带到床上。或者你在周日准备了餐食，坚持在家吃健康的晚餐，但到了周五，你发现自己太累了，选择了点油腻的外卖。生活就是这样，即使你的行为改变很小，每一天都可能相当不灵活，在某个时候你的运气可能会用完，即使只是一天。你内心的完美主义者可能会尖叫着完全放弃目标，但试着从大局来看。仅仅因为你可能暂时偏离轨道，并不意味着你第二天不能重新开始。

paragraphs.text: The final one to avoid is discounting small progress. There's a habit that many perfectionists tend to fall into when they try to establish a behavior change. They focus too much on the big goal and don't take the time to celebrate the small progress they make in the process. Your brain responds to rewards. The basal ganglia, the brain region linked to our performance of habits, is most active at the beginning of a behavior, when the habit is cured, and at the end, when it's rewarded. Say your goal is to run five miles three times a week, and this week you ran one mile on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Rather than focusing on how far you've gone toward your goal, think about how you can reward yourself for the progress you've made. It doesn't have to be big or expensive; it can be something as simple as making your favorite fruit juice after your run. Whatever your reward, it has to be more than just the activity itself to get you going.
paragraphs.translation: 最后一个要避免的是低估小进步。当许多完美主义者试图建立行为改变时，他们往往会陷入一种习惯。他们过于关注大目标，而没有花时间庆祝过程中取得的小进步。你的大脑对奖励有反应。基底神经节，与我们习惯表现相关的大脑区域，在行为开始时（当习惯被培养时）和结束时（当获得奖励时）最为活跃。假设你的目标是每周跑步三次，每次五英里，而本周你在周一、周三和周五各跑了一英里。与其专注于你离目标还有多远，不如想想如何奖励自己取得的进步。它不必很大或很昂贵；它可以像跑完步后制作你最喜欢的果汁一样简单。无论你的奖励是什么，它必须不仅仅是活动本身，才能让你继续前进。

paragraphs.text: Initiating a new behavior usually seems like the hardest part of the process of change. However, people often fail to adequately prepare for maintaining it. One of the reasons for this is because we mistakenly believe the strategies we used to initiate the change will be equally effective in helping us continue the change. But they won't. Where changing a strongly deep-rooted habit requires changing our belief about that habit that penetrates deeply into our lives, continually manifesting that wisdom requires that we maintain a positive outlook. If our mood is low, the wisdom to behave differently seems to disappear and we go back to eating more and exercising less. The key, then, to maintaining new behaviors is to be happy! Which is why it's so hard to maintain new behaviors.
paragraphs.translation: 启动一个新行为通常看起来是改变过程中最难的部分。然而，人们往往未能充分准备维持它。其中一个原因是我们错误地认为，我们用来启动改变的策略在帮助我们继续改变时同样有效。但它们不会。改变一个根深蒂固的习惯需要改变我们对那个习惯的信念，这种信念渗透到我们生活的深处，持续体现这种智慧需要我们保持积极的心态。如果我们的情绪低落，行为不同的智慧似乎就消失了，我们又回到吃得多、运动少的状态。那么，维持新行为的关键是要快乐！这就是为什么维持新行为如此困难。

paragraphs.text: Remember, overcoming the behavioral inertia that prevents us from implementing new changes, like eating a healthy diet or exercising, can benefit us in the long run and can improve our physical and mental health. No one was born with habits. They were all learned, and can all, therefore, be unlearned. The question is: how badly do you really want to change?

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: The "American Dream" promises that in the Land of Opportunity, any individual can climb the economic ladder and prosper through hard work and ambition alone. And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations. So why does the idea of the American Dream persist? A new study in the American Journal of Political Science identifies one factor that has been overlooked: the influence of reality TV. Reality shows have come to dominate US television over the past 20 years, notes Eunji Kim from Vanderbilt University. And the overwhelming majority of these have a "rags-to-riches" storyline: they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success. And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts—which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans—get a much smaller proportion of the viewership. Rags-to-riches stories are ubiquitous on TV—but does watching these programmes actually convince people that economic mobility is easily attainable? To find out, Kim's team had participants watch a 5-minute clip from a reality show with a rags-to-riches storyline. Control participants watched a clip from a reality show that didn't have a rags-to-riches story. After watching the shows, participants rated how much they agreed with four statements relating to the American Dream. The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream. Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs. Kim also conducted a survey of 3,000 US residents. They also rated the extent to which they believed success in life is related to various internal factors (such as ambition) and external factors (such as family wealth). Finally, they read a list of TV programmes and indicated which they regularly watched. Participants who were heavy viewers of rags-to-riches programmes or frequent viewers had a stronger belief in the American Dream than those who never watched such shows. Kim concludes that "rags-to-riches entertainment media are an important cultural force that promotes and perpetuates beliefs in upward mobility". And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality. "In this era of choice, entertainment media are what captures hearts and minds," Kim writes. "Its political consequences are anything but trivial".
paragraphs.translation: “美国梦”承诺，在机会之地，任何个体都可以仅凭努力工作和雄心壮志攀登经济阶梯并取得成功。然而，今天的美国年轻人正努力在相同年龄比他们的父母挣得更多，而美国的向上流动性实际上不如其他工业化国家。那么，为什么美国梦的理念依然持续存在？《美国政治学杂志》上的一项新研究发现了一个被忽视的因素：真人秀电视的影响。范德比尔特大学的 Eunji Kim 指出，在过去20年里，真人秀节目已经主导了美国电视。而绝大多数这类节目都有“白手起家”的故事情节：它们以普通美国人努力工作取得巨大经济成功为特色。虽然这些节目经常是收视率最高的节目之一，但新闻广播——描绘了数百万美国人面临经济困难的更现实景象——收视份额要小得多。白手起家的故事在电视上无处不在——但观看这些节目真的能让人们相信经济流动性很容易实现吗？为了找出答案，Kim 的团队让参与者观看一段5分钟的具有白手起家故事情节的真人秀片段。对照组参与者观看了一段没有白手起家故事的真人秀片段。观看节目后，参与者评价了他们对四个与美国梦相关的陈述的同意程度。结果表明，观看白手起家片段的人确实对美国梦有显著更强的信念。有趣的是，当参与者按党派归属分组时，这种效应在共和党人中显著，但在民主党人中不显著，这表明这些电视节目中隐含的信息可能迎合了人们现有的社会经济信念。Kim 还对3,000名美国居民进行了调查。他们还评价了他们认为生活中的成功与各种内部因素（如雄心）和外部因素（如家庭财富）相关的程度。最后，他们阅读了一份电视节目列表，并指出了他们经常观看哪些节目。经常观看白手起家节目或频繁观看的参与者比从未观看此类节目的人对美国梦有更强的信念。Kim 总结道：“白手起家的娱乐媒体是促进和延续向上流动性信念的重要文化力量。”问题在于：如果人们错误地相信，努力工作就是个人为自己创造更好生活所需的全部，他们可能对那些能真正减少不平等的政策支持度较低。“在这个选择的时代，娱乐媒体是捕获人心的东西，”Kim 写道。“其政治后果绝非微不足道。”

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: When someone asks us 'what do you do?' We nearly always reply with our occupation. Work, for many of us, is much more than a job. It is the defining aspect of our identity. For many of us it is through our job that we can define ourselves. "Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself. One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance. If we take the time to reflect we might recognise that as well as our work we can also identify as a friend, a spouse, a son or daughter, a parent, a member of a sports team or religious community. We may recognise that we feel and act differently in these roles and relationships than we do at work. The passive daughter becomes an assertive leader at work. Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time. I myself have been a shop assistant, a waitress, a student, a graduate, and a clinical psychologist. At each stage my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing. Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market. How we see ourselves is central to the issue of our identity. When we tell ourselves "I'm good at starting projects but not so great at seeing them through" it can become part of our belief system. But if you have the unfortunate experience of an enforced job change you will need to examine those beliefs to see how grounded in reality they are. You will be required to ask yourself how helpful these beliefs are and consider personal change. We can change our beliefs, behaviours and emotional experience at any time through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline. In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options. Ultimately it is you who define who you are. You are only your job if you let it be so.
paragraphs.translation: 当有人问我们“你是做什么的？”我们几乎总是以职业来回答。工作，对我们许多人来说，远不止是一份工作。它是我们身份的定义性方面。对我们许多人来说，正是通过工作，我们才能定义自己。“没有工作，我不知道我是谁，”这句话在我的办公椅上不止一次被说出。确实，与那些失去或被迫改变工作的客户一起工作时，这可能是最具挑战性的方面之一。这种丧失引发的身份危机远大于失去工作本身。然而，我逐渐理解的一点是，我们的身份比我们第一眼看到的要复杂得多。如果我们花时间反思，我们可能会意识到，除了工作，我们还可以认同自己是朋友、配偶、儿子或女儿、父母、体育队或宗教社区的成员。我们可能认识到，在这些角色和关系中，我们的感受和行为与在工作中不同。被动的女儿在工作中变成了自信的领导者。此外，我们在工作中的身份不是静态的。它们随着时间而变化。我自己曾当过店员、女服务员、学生、毕业生和临床心理学家。在每个阶段，我适应和发展职业身份的能力对我的幸福感至关重要。虽然我们喜欢消除生活中的不确定性，但在某种程度上，我们必须管理不确定性，尤其是在当今动荡和不断变化的就业市场中。我们如何看待自己是身份问题的核心。当我们告诉自己“我擅长启动项目，但不太擅长坚持到底”时，这可能成为我们信念系统的一部分。但如果你不幸经历了强制性的工作变动，你需要审视这些信念，看看它们在多大程度上基于现实。你需要问自己这些信念有多有用，并考虑个人改变。我们可以通过实验、实践和有意识的自律，随时改变我们的信念、行为和情感体验。在一个职业生涯可能将我们带入新领域的时代，挑战自我意识并探索是否可以通过改变对自己的信念来创造新的身份体验，以扩展职业选择，变得越来越重要。归根结底，是你定义了你是谁。只有当你让它如此时，工作才定义了你。

questionGroups.sourceText: 中国盛产竹子，是最早开发利用竹资源的国家。竹子在中国分布广泛，品种丰富。竹子实用性强，用于生产和生活的许多方面，如筷子、桌椅的制作和桥梁、房屋的建造。中国人爱竹，自古以来就有无数文人以竹为主题，创作了绚丽多彩的文学和绘画作品。竹子主干(stem) 笔直，象征正直的品格。竹子具有强大的生命力和适应能力，无论环境多么恶劣，都能够顽强生存，因而寓意坚韧不拔的精神。几千年来，竹子一直被视为中华民族品格的象征。

answer.modelTranslation: China is rich in bamboo and is one of the earliest countries to develop and utilize bamboo resources. Bamboo is widely distributed and diverse in varieties across China. It is highly practical and used in many aspects of production and daily life, such as the making of chopsticks, tables and chairs, and the construction of bridges and houses. The Chinese have a fondness for bamboo; since ancient times, countless literati have used bamboo as a theme to create a rich and colorful array of literature and paintings. The bamboo's stem is straight, symbolizing upright character. Bamboo possesses strong vitality and adaptability, surviving tenaciously in harsh environments, thus embodying the spirit of resilience. For thousands of years, bamboo has been regarded as a symbol of the Chinese nation's character.
